messages.author: c6c2f8b68485ba9a
messages.subject: Issues regarding Profile likelihood plotting
parts:
Dear Dr. Efford,

I have run secr for my data set (5 seasons pooled together) to estimate season specific density. Now I was trying to plot the profile likelihood for secr models. Unfortunately, I am getting this error message while running the code, please check:


> outPL <- pmixProfileLL(rtrall, mask= rtrmask, model = list(D~session, g0~h2, sigma~h2), trace = TRUE, pmvals, CL = F, pmi = 0.5, pmindx= 4, binomN= 1, start = list(D=5, g0= 0.05, sigma= 2068))
Checking data
Preparing detection design matrices
Preparing density design matrix
Finding initial parameter values...
Initial values  D = 0.00041, g0 = 0.00202, sigma = 2375.86881
Error in (function (capthist, model = list(D ~ 1, g0 ~ 1, sigma ~ 1),  :
  invalid fixed beta - require NP-vector
In addition: Warning message:
In autoini(ch, msk, binomN = details$binomN, ignoreusage = details$ignoreusage) :
  'autoini' failed to find g0; setting initial g0 = 0.1
>




Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks.

Regards,

Ayan Sadhu

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Issues regarding Profile likelihood plotting
parts:
Dear Ayan

Do you really want to do this? See the Note in the help file.

The help file says 'Choosing the wrong value for pmi results in the error message "invalid fixed beta - require NP-vector".'

It also says pmi should be an integer (0.5 is not an integer). Quite likely you should use pmi = 9, but I cannot say for sure.

The argument pmindx in your code is an error (pmixProfileLL has no such argument), but that may have had no effect.

Murray

messages.subject: Re: Issues regarding Profile likelihood plotting
parts:
Dear Dr. Efford,

Thank you very much for your inputs. I was using this code, as I suspect there was some problem with model merging. Every time I am estimating the density season-wise, I am getting different estimates,
e.g., for the same season's density estimate,
1st run: 0.1072/sq. km
2nd run: 0.0748/sq. km

I have changed the 'pmi' value to 10, but can you please give me more insight regarding the use of it. I was going through the help file pdfs, but got confused with this particular parameter.

As you correctly suggested, 'pmindx' has nothing to do with it, but somehow it was creating problem while running the code. Now its running perfectly...waiting for the plots to come.

Thank you!

Regards,

Ayan Sadhu

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Issues regarding Profile likelihood plotting
parts:
OK, that is odd behaviour, and I can see why you might suspect that the estimates differed because each run was ending up on a different mode of the likelihood. That is possible with mixture models. The 'pmi' argument identifies which one of the beta parameters corresponds to 'pmix'. Perhaps it should be able to find this automatically (I can't remember why that doesn't always work). I hope pmixProfileLL gives some insight.
Murray

parts:
Dear Dr. Efford,

As the pmicProfileLL is still running, I could not ascertain you regarding the output. It is already more than two days (>30 hours) the analysis is going on. While running the analysis, I have inserted the initial values for D, g0, and sigma in the code, is it creating some problems in the analysis?

Additionally, I need your suggestion regarding pooling of the data for this analysis. The data I am using is consists of five trapping sessions (years), and for the analysis, I have pooled all the years and instructed 'secr' for session-wise density estimates. According to your expertise, is it a good way to deal with such data? Shall I go for individual session (year) models, so that I can avoid the issue of model merging (which is prevalent in the case of pooled analysis)?

Thank you for your time and insights.

With warm regards,

Ayan Sadhu
